question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

My son was not well yesterday and today I'm **feeling sick**.
solution: The correct answer is** Option 1)** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The phrase **"Under the weather"** means feeling ill or unwell. (अस्वस्थ होना) • **Example: **She has been **under the weather** for a few days, so she decided to see a doctor. • **"Feeling unwell"** means not feeling good and healthy • **Example: **She said she **was feeling unwell** and went home. Therefore, the correct idiom of the given phrase is '**Under the weather**.' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Call it a day** (दिन का काम समाप्त करना): Stopping work for the day. • **Example: **After working for 12 hours straight, I decided to **call it a day.** • **Face the music** (परिणामों का सामना करना): To confront the consequences of one's actions. • **Example: **After failing the exam, he had to** face the music **when he got home. • **Break a leg** (शुभकामनाएँ देना): A way to wish someone good luck, especially before a performance. • **Example: **Before the play began, the director told the cast to** break a leg.** 35:Tab9, The correct answer is **Option 1)**
